design.rules: Heads-up hold'em river drill. You are Seat 0. Seat 1 is the same opponent throughout the session. Each deal starts on the river with 10 bb in the pot, 5 bb contributed by each player. Seat 1 has checked. In this drill Seat 1 is dealt exactly one pair of the board's highest rank. You may check or bet 10 bb. Seat 1 may call or fold. Maximize expected chips.
design.read_prompt: Estimate the probability that Seat 1 folds to the next pot-sized river bet, using only the supplied observations. Every listed bet gave Seat 1 a choice of call or fold. A probability of 80 means 80 percent of such bets get folded. Give your best estimate of current behavior. Return only the requested JSON object.

note_prompts.observations: Record observed calls and folds by Seat 1, with counts and when they occurred. Keep observations only. Write at most 80 words.
note_prompts.advice: Record observed calls and folds by Seat 1, with counts and when they occurred. Recommend how to play against Seat 1. Write at most 80 words.

design.primary: Post-phase-2 probe loss for direct versus read-then-bet, by notebook format.
design.unit: One observed tape per condition; descriptive pilot only.
design.exposure: Predetermined pot bets, same responses for both notebook writers.
design.host_baseline: Recent six bets, (folds+1)/(bets+2), rounded to nearest 5 percent.
design.controls: Frozen notes and predictions, blank, true current fold probability.
design.cache: Identical requests reuse their first answer at temperature zero.

measurement_caveat: The legacy reader restricts percentage strings to five-point buckets without a rounding instruction. This can distort answers such as 8.3 into 80 or 85. These reader outputs do not establish a reading failure. Betting actions are preserved, but read-then-bet scores depend on this encoding. See the numeric replay runner.
